note: The frozen half of the task. Nothing a submission says may move any number in this file. The verifier reads its OWN copy of it at grading time, and tests/Dockerfile refuses to build unless the two copies are byte-identical.

architecture.note: Rotary position encoding, so the decoder is defined at every sequence length up to max_seq_len and the same parameters serve every geometry a plan may name. That is what makes the sequence length a FREE variable here instead of an architectural constant.

budget.note: The compute budget is fixed in TOKENS, not in optimizer steps and not in wall clock. It was SIZED BY MEASUREMENT: the graded pass trains three models over it from scratch, and this figure is what keeps that pass inside the grading envelope on a shared H100. Every plan consumes exactly this many training tokens in exactly this order, so every plan costs the same number of token-forward and token-backward passes. What a plan chooses is the SHAPE those tokens are fed in -- how many rows, how long each row is, and how many micro-batches accumulate into one optimizer step -- and therefore how many optimizer steps the same tokens buy and how much context each token is predicted from.

geometry.note: rows * seq_len is the micro-batch token count and is held between min_microbatch_tokens and max_microbatch_tokens so that no plan can be much slower per token than any other. rows * seq_len * grad_accum is the optimizer-step token count, and total_train_tokens divided by it is how many optimizer steps that phase buys.

optimizer.name: AdamW
optimizer.note: FROZEN. These four per-role peak learning rates and every AdamW constant are fixed by the task and no plan may move them. This slot does not grade optimizer tuning; it grades batch geometry.

schedule.note: FROZEN, and deliberately clocked in TOKENS CONSUMED rather than in optimizer steps. A schedule read off a step index would hand a plan with fewer, larger steps a different envelope than a plan with more, smaller ones, and the comparison would then be about the schedule rather than about the geometry. Clocked in tokens, every plan sees the same peak-relative multiplier at the same point of the same token budget. On top of that envelope the peak is scaled by sqrt(optimizer_step_tokens / batch_scaling_reference_tokens), the standard square-root rule for adaptive optimizers, so a plan that accumulates into larger steps is not simply handed a smaller total parameter movement. Both rules are frozen and applied by the harness; neither is a number a plan may set.

init.note: Every run in this task starts from the same parameter tensors. The batch-geometry plan is the only thing that differs between two runs.

evaluation.metric: mean token-level cross entropy in nats, lower is better
evaluation.note: The evaluation geometry is FIXED at 16 x 512 for every run, whatever geometry a plan trained under. A plan is scored on the loss it produces at one fixed reading geometry, so a plan cannot win by moving the measurement. The graded split is NOT in the agent image: environment/data/devset_slice.bin is a proxy cut from a different training shard and is the agent's own yardstick.

data.format: FineWeb10B GPT-2 BPE. 1024-byte int32 header (magic 20240520, version 1, token count), then uint16 token ids.
data.train_slice_note: The stream is consumed strictly in order from position 0 and every plan consumes exactly total_train_tokens of it, so two plans see the same tokens in the same order and differ only in how those tokens were grouped.
